candidates.name: s3-notification-on-unowned-bucket
candidates.curator_note: OPERATOR NOTE: Terraform is arguably WORSE here — it has no custom-resource UPSERT for existing bucket notifications; adding notification config to a bucket that already has notifications easily creates flip-flop infra across resource owners. Re-examine this candidate's arm prediction before speccing.
candidates.comment: Terraform is even worse here as it can't provide a custom resource to UPSERT existing bucket notification - adding bucket notification configuration to an existing bucket with bucket notifications is very easy to create flip-flop infra across resource owners
features: Needs a pre-seeded, agent-unowned fixture: a bucket created OUT OF BAND (by the harness, before the trial) already carrying one notification. The generator has no 'pre-provisioned AWS fixture' concept today — iam-e2e-role's fixtures are the closest precedent; this needs a documented seed+teardown step and a name handed to the agent via the instruction.

A 'no extra resources of type X' assertion primitive that reads identically on both oracles (cfn-guard: count AWS::Lambda::Function == expected; Rego: count aws_lambda_function == expected). Worth building once — it is the generic shape for every custom-resource-tax scenario.
Live teardown must remove the notification from the seeded bucket before deleting it, or the sandwiched fixture leaks.

candidates.comment: should not allow secrets in iac
features: awscdk arm has no CloudFormation resource-schema linter (cfn-lint / registry schema validation) — without one, a schema-invalid template sails through tier 0 and tier 1 and the tier-attribution row is unfairly generous to the CDK arm. Either add cfn-lint 1.x to arms/awscdk/environment/Dockerfile (alongside the existing cfn-guard 3.2.0) or pre-register that this scenario is live-only.

candidates.name: acm-cert-cross-region-for-cloudfront
candidates.comment: aws-bench scp restricts trials to a single region. keep for backlog
features: BLOCKER: the awscdk arm's output_contract assumes exactly one synthesized template (`artifact_path: cdk.out/ScenarioStack.template.json`, per specs/apigw-openapi.yaml). A correct CDK solution here is a multi-stack app; the generator, the trajectory-audit gate and the cfn-guard invocation all need a multi-artifact mode (glob of cdk.out/*.template.json, policy applied across the set). This is the largest toolkit change requested by any candidate in this shard, and it unlocks every future cross-region/cross-stack scenario.

hcl-raw and terraconstructs arms need credentials valid in two regions — same account, same admin role, so no new AWS setup, but the offline/mock-STS preflight (arms/terraconstructs/environment/app/mock-sts.js) must tolerate a second aliased provider.

Region policy: DECISIONS.md pins the sandbox to us-east-1. This scenario deliberately needs a non-us-east-1 workload region. Static/plan-only means nothing is created outside us-east-1, but the pre-registration should be amended explicitly rather than silently.

candidates.name: rds-blue-green-deployment
candidates.comment: terraconstructs hasn't landed L2 constructs for RDS (it is part of stacked open PRs) - arm may be able to succeed due to L1 binding for now, but scenario is valuable to eval when RDS support does land.
features: SLOW RESOURCE — hard blocker against the stated ~20 min live budget. An RDS instance takes 10-15 min to create before the blue/green deployment even starts, then the green environment provisions and the switchover runs; realistic wall clock is 40-60 min. This needs either a per-scenario live-budget override with its own justification, or a pre-provisioned long-lived blue instance in the sandbox that trials attach to (which then needs its own lifecycle, cost accounting and contamination story between trials).
Cost: the only candidate in this shard with non-trivial AWS spend.
